description: Experience the comforting warmth of Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, a staple in Middle Eastern cuisine. This hearty and wholesome soup is packed with vibrant flavors from fresh lemon, aromatic spices, and nutritious red lentils, making it a perfect meal for any season. Enjoy a taste of authentic Lebanon with every spoonful of this traditional and satisfying dish.

instructions.title: Prepare Ingredients
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear, then drain them. Chop the onion, mince the garlic, and dice the carrot and potato into small, uniform pieces to ensure even cooking.

instructions.title: Sauté Aromatics
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until it becomes soft and translucent. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant, being careful not to burn it.

instructions.title: Add Vegetables and Spices
instructions.text: Stir in the diced carrot and potato, cooking for 3-5 minutes to slightly soften them. Add the ground cumin, turmeric powder, salt, and black pepper. Stir well to coat the vegetables and cook for 1 minute until the spices are aromatic.

instructions.title: Combine with Lentils and Broth
instructions.text: Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot, then pour in the vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils and vegetables are very tender.

instructions.title: Blend to Desired Consistency
instructions.text: Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it reaches your desired consistency. For a smoother soup, blend longer; for a chunkier texture, blend less. Alternatively, you can transfer portions of the soup to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot.

instructions.title: Finish and Serve
instructions.text: Stir in the fresh lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning with more salt, pepper, or lemon juice as needed. Ladle the hot Lebanese Red Lentil Soup into bowls, garnish with fresh chopped cilantro, and serve immediately with a drizzle of olive oil or a side of pita bread.

tips: For a richer flavor, consider a quick drizzle of good quality extra virgin olive oil just before serving.
If you prefer a thicker soup, you can mash some of the potatoes against the side of the pot or simmer uncovered for a few extra minutes to reduce.
Leftover Adas soup stores beautifully in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days, and can also be frozen for longer storage.
article:
Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas (pronounced "ah-das"), is more than just a dish; it's a warm hug in a bowl, a staple in Middle Eastern homes, and a testament to the power of simple, wholesome ingredients. This vibrant, comforting soup has nourished generations, offering a perfect blend of earthy flavors, rich texture, and incredible health benefits. Whether you're seeking a quick, nutritious meal on a busy weeknight or a comforting remedy on a cold day, Adas is a culinary gem that deserves a place in your repertoire of Middle Eastern Soups and Stews. Its bright color, thanks to the red lentils, and its signature tang from fresh lemon juice make it irresistibly appealing and deeply satisfying.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Adas)?

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, or Adas, is a beloved vegan and gluten-free soup that holds a special place in Lebanese and broader Middle Eastern cuisine. At its heart, it’s a simple yet incredibly flavorful creation made primarily from red lentils, aromatic vegetables like onions and garlic, and a generous squeeze of fresh lemon juice. Unlike some other lentil soups, Adas typically has a smoother, often creamy consistency, achieved by simmering the lentils until they break down, sometimes with a quick blend.

Historically, lentils have been a cornerstone of diets across the Middle East for millennia, prized for their affordability, nutritional value, and versatility. Adas embodies this tradition, serving as a frugal yet highly nourishing meal, packed with protein, fiber, and essential minerals. It's frequently enjoyed during colder months, as a light lunch, or as an appetizer for a larger meal. The beauty of this Lebanese Red Lentil Soup lies in its unpretentious nature and its ability to deliver profound comfort and robust flavor with minimal fuss. It’s a dish that truly showcases how humble ingredients can be transformed into something extraordinary.

## Ingredients You Need for Adas Soup

Creating an authentic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup doesn't require an extensive shopping list. The magic lies in the quality of these few, key components:

*   **Red Lentils:** 1 cup, dried. These cook quickly and break down easily, giving the soup its characteristic creamy texture and vibrant color. Make sure to rinse them thoroughly before use.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped. Provides the aromatic base and sweetness.
*   **Garlic:** 3-4 cloves, minced. Adds a pungent depth of flavor that is quintessential to Lebanese cooking.
*   **Vegetable Broth or Water:** 6-8 cups. While water works perfectly, a good quality vegetable broth will enhance the overall flavor.
*   **Olive Oil:** 2-3 tablespoons, for sautéing and drizzling. Use extra virgin olive oil for the best flavor.
*   **Lemon:** 1-2 medium, fresh. The juice is crucial for balancing the richness of the lentils and providing the signature bright, tangy finish. Don't skip this!
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To taste. Essential for seasoning.
*   **Optional Garnishes:** Fresh parsley or cilantro (chopped), a pinch of dried mint, extra drizzle of olive oil, and lemon wedges for serving.

## Step-by-Step Instructions to Make Lebanese Red Lentil Soup

Making this heartwarming Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is a straightforward process, even for novice cooks.

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Start by rinsing your red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris and helps prevent the soup from becoming cloudy. Set aside.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes, or until softened and translucent, being careful not to brown them too much.
3.  **Add Garlic:** Stir in the minced garlic and cook for another 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Be mindful not to burn the garlic, as this can make it bitter.
4.  **Combine and Simmer:** Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot, along with 6 cups of vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover the pot, and let it simmer for 20-25 minutes. The lentils should become very soft and begin to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Achieve Desired Consistency:** At this point, you can choose your preferred texture. For a rustic soup, you can leave it as is or mash some of the lentils against the side of the pot with a spoon. For a smoother, creamier soup, carefully use an immersion blender directly in the pot, or transfer portions to a regular blender (blending in batches and being careful with hot liquids) until smooth. If the soup is too thick, add more broth or hot water until you reach your desired consistency.
6.  **Season and Finish:** Return the soup to the stove if you used a regular blender. Stir in the juice of one lemon, and season generously with salt and black pepper to taste. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed – you might want more lemon juice or a pinch more salt.
7.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot soup into bowls. Garnish with a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil, a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or cilantro, and a wedge of lemon on the side for an extra burst of freshness.

## Pro Tips for the Best Adas Soup

Elevating your Lebanese Red Lentil Soup from good to exceptional is all about these little details:

*   **Fresh Lemon is Non-Negotiable:** The bright, tangy flavor of fresh lemon juice is what truly defines Adas. Bottled lemon juice simply won't yield the same vibrant taste. Don't be shy; add more lemon juice to your personal preference at the end.
*   **Don't Overlook the Olive Oil:** A good quality extra virgin olive oil for both sautéing and a final drizzle makes a significant difference. It adds a fruity, peppery note that enhances the overall richness.
*   **Season as You Go (and at the End):** Taste your soup throughout the cooking process. Lentils absorb a lot of salt, so a final adjustment after simmering and adding lemon juice is crucial.
*   **Immersion Blender for Creaminess:** While optional, an immersion blender makes achieving that silky, creamy texture incredibly easy and mess-free. If you prefer a heartier, chunkier soup, skip the blending entirely.
*   **Consider a Pinch of Cumin:** While not always traditional in Lebanese Adas, a small pinch (1/4 teaspoon) of ground cumin added with the garlic can lend a subtle, earthy warmth that many enjoy in Middle Eastern lentil soups.
*   **Fresh Herbs for Brightness:** A sprinkle of fresh parsley or cilantro just before serving adds a beautiful color contrast and a burst of fresh flavor. Dried mint is another traditional topping that adds a unique aromatic touch.

## Serving Suggestions for Lebanese Lentil Soup

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is wonderfully versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways. Traditionally, it's served hot and fresh, often as a light meal in itself or as a starter.

*   **With Crusty Bread:** The most classic pairing is with warm pita bread or any crusty bread, perfect for dipping and soaking up every last drop of the flavorful broth.
*   **Alongside a Simple Salad:** A crisp green salad dressed with a lemon-tahini dressing or a simple vinaigrette provides a refreshing contrast to the hearty soup.
*   **Extra Lemon Wedges:** Always offer extra lemon wedges on the side, allowing each diner to customize the tanginess to their liking.
*   **A Drizzle of Olive Oil:** A final swirl of good quality extra virgin olive oil not only adds richness but also a beautiful sheen to the soup.
*   **Spicy Kick:** For those who enjoy a bit of heat, a pinch of red pepper flakes or a dash of hot sauce can be added to individual bowls.
*   **Pickles and Olives:** A small side dish of Middle Eastern pickles (like pickled turnips or cucumbers) and olives makes for an authentic accompaniment, adding briny notes that complement the soup.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Adas recipe is perfect as is, there are several ways to customize this Lebanese Red Lentil Soup to suit different tastes or dietary needs:

*   **Add Vegetables:** For an even more nutritious soup, consider adding finely diced carrots, celery, or potatoes along with the onions and garlic. They will soften and meld into the soup beautifully.
*   **Spice It Up:** Beyond the optional cumin, you could experiment with a pinch of turmeric for extra color and earthy notes, or a dash of Lebanese 7-spice blend for a more complex aroma.
*   **Greens Power-Up:** Stir in a handful of fresh spinach or Swiss chard during the last 5 minutes of cooking for added nutrients and a lovely green hue.
*   **Vegan Creaminess:** While already vegan, for an extra creamy texture without dairy, a splash of coconut milk or cashew cream can be stirred in at the very end.
*   **Garlic Confit:** For a milder, sweeter garlic flavor, you can slowly confit the garlic in olive oil before adding it to the soup, or even roast whole heads of garlic and squeeze out the softened cloves.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** A pinch of smoked paprika can add a subtle smoky depth that complements the earthy lentils.

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Adas) is a testament to the idea that the most satisfying meals often come from the simplest ingredients. Its comforting warmth, nutritional benefits, and bright, tangy flavor make it a perennial favorite. Whether you're a seasoned cook or just starting your culinary journey, mastering this dish will bring a taste of authentic Lebanese hospitality right into your kitchen. So, gather your ingredients and prepare to fall in love with this humble yet extraordinary Middle Eastern classic.
